blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Current controllable video generation systems often rely on 2D motion
trajectories or sparse drag signals for object motion. These controls
are ambiguous because the same 2D trajectory can correspond to different
3D motions, especially when the camera and objects move simultaneously.
We present Generative Cinematographer (GenCine), a system that
lifts a single image into an editable 3D scene scaffold where artists
jointly author camera and foreground motion. Artists specify a camera
path and move selected foreground regions using local 3D motion handles.
Several handles can move different parts of a subject independently,
providing a piecewise-rigid approximation to non-rigid motion without
a physics simulator or category-specific prior. To communicate these
controls to a pretrained video model, we project them into guidance maps.
These maps record where the controlled regions appear in each frame,
assign each handle a fixed color across frames and encode the
current 3D positions of its controlled points in the same world
coordinate system as the background. This lets us
describe object motion relative to the scene even as the camera moves.
For training, we recover controls from the motion observed in real
videos and use ground-truth geometry and trajectories from synthetic
videos. We train a lightweight guidance branch and LoRA adapters on a
pretrained Wan model to follow these controls. Our experiments show consistent camera-relative
motion, improved geometric consistency under viewpoint changes,
and strong controllability across diverse real-world scenes.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
“Just as one can compose colors, or forms,
so one can compose motions.” — Alexander Calder (1933) Composing a cinematic shot means deciding how the camera and the subjects
move together. Classical graphics systems such as the Virtual
Cinematographer ( He et al., 1996 ) compose shots by controlling a camera
within a modeled 3D scene. We bring this world-space approach to video
generation, allowing artists to jointly author camera and object motion
using a 3D scaffold lifted from a single image (Fig. 1 ).
Generative video models can now synthesize plausible motion from a single
image, but giving artists precise control over these movements remains
difficult. Text prompts can describe an action but
leave its precise path unspecified. Likewise, a 2D drag may correspond
to several 3D motions or mix object movement with a change in viewpoint
(Fig. 2 ). A generated video can therefore look plausible
while following a different motion from the one the artist intended.

blocks.en:
Many controllable video methods specify foreground motion through pixel
displacements ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Geng et al., 2024 ) , leaving
the underlying 3D motion implicit. Physics simulators and category-specific
priors provide additional structure ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025b ) ,
but their applicability depends on the materials and objects they support.
Learning 3D control from videos presents a further challenge: reliable
3D motion annotations are scarce. Synthetic data provide these annotations
but differ visually from real footage, while per-pixel 2D
conditioning ( Chu et al., 2025 ) leaves artists working in image space.

blocks.en:
A natural way to express the intended motion is to place the camera and
subjects in a shared 3D scene. Camera paths then describe how the viewpoint
changes, while object trajectories describe how the scene itself changes.
We follow this approach in Generative Cinematographer (GenCine). Starting
from a single image, we lift the scene into a colored point cloud.
The artist selects a few foreground regions and specifies how each
should move in 3D, along with a camera path. Each selected region acts
as a motion handle : its points move together as a rigid group.
Several handles can move different parts of a subject independently,
providing a piecewise-rigid approximation to non-rigid motion without
a skeleton, physics simulator, or category-specific prior.

To train the model, we recover examples of the motion an artist might specify.
For real videos, 3D foundation models estimate geometry and camera motion.
We use these estimates to lift tracked foreground points into 3D, group
nearby tracks into local handles, and use their observed motion as
approximate 3D controls. Synthetic videos supply ground-truth geometry
and trajectories. Each clip is thus paired with controls describing the
motion that actually occurs in it; its first frame supplies the reference
image, and the clip supplies the target video.

blocks.en:
A pretrained video model does not directly interpret a camera path or
a collection of 3D point trajectories. We need a representation that
fits its image-based input while retaining what the controls mean.
Recent methods support joint camera and object
control ( Zheng et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ) ;
VerseCrafter, for example, uses RGB and depth maps of a background point
cloud and object-level Gaussian trajectories. Our representation
separates three questions: where does a region appear, which
region is it, and how does it move in the world? First, we view the scene through the specified camera at each frame,
placing guidance at the projected locations of background and handle
points. Second, a fixed color identifies each handle across frames.
Third, separate colors encode the current 3D positions of foreground
points and the fixed positions of background points. These form the
foreground identity, foreground XYZ, and background XYZ maps.
The two XYZ maps use the same world frame and scale: camera motion
changes where a static point appears, whereas object motion also changes
its world position. This distinction preserves information that a 2D
trajectory alone discards.

blocks.en:
We construct these guidance sequences for each training clip and encode
them with the pretrained video model’s frozen video autoencoder.
The diffusion model learns to generate the paired video from its first
frame, text, and encoded guidance. We train a lightweight side branch
and LoRA adapters while keeping the base model weights frozen, allowing
the model to learn control without retraining its visual prior.
At inference, an artist’s camera path and handle trajectories pass
through the same map construction in place of recovered motion.
Varying the number and placement of training handles exposes the model
to the sparse, partial controls available during authoring.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are:
(1) a visual guidance representation for 3D motion that preserves handle identity and foreground–background positions in a shared world frame while remaining compatible with pretrained video models;
(2) a local 3D motion-handle formulation that approximates non-rigid motion through independently controlled local rigid regions, without requiring a simulator or category-specific prior; and
(3) a shared training and authoring pipeline that learns from videos paired with 3D motion controls and generates videos from a single image using artist-authored camera paths and local object trajectories.
2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: The graphics community has long studied camera motion authoring. The Virtual Cinematographer ( He et al., 1996 ) formalized shot composition as cinematographic idioms. Later work extended this to declarative camera planning ( Christianson et al., 1996 ) and procedural camera control ( Drucker et al., 1992 ) . These systems assume a fully modeled 3D scene. In contrast, GenCine uses a 3D scaffold lifted from a single image to control the video generator.
blocks.zh: 图形社区长期研究相机运动作曲. 虚拟电影制片人(He等人,1996年)正式将镜头组成成电影的平面。 后来的工作将这项工作扩大到宣布相机规划(Christianson等人,1996年)和程序相机控制(Drucker等人,1992年)。 这些系统假设一个完全模型化的3D场景. 相形之下,GenCine使用从单一图像上抬起的3D脚手架来控制视频生成器.

blocks.en:
MotionCtrl ( Wang et al., 2024 ) and CameraCtrl ( He et al., 2025a ; He et al., 2025b ) condition generation on camera poses.
GEN3C ( Ren et al., 2025 ) renders a depth-derived 3D cache under target poses, while DimensionX ( Sun et al., 2025 ) generates 3D and 4D scenes from one image.
WorldReel ( Fang et al., 2025 ) jointly generates RGB frames, point maps, camera trajectories, and flow for geometric and motion consistency.
Generative Camera Dolly ( Van Hoorick et al., 2024 ) , TrajectoryCrafter ( Yu et al., 2025 ) , and FreeOrbit4D ( Cao et al., 2026 ) redirect viewpoints in existing videos, with FreeOrbit4D reconstructing a geometry-complete 4D proxy.
Vista4D ( Lin et al., 2026 ) reshoots source videos using rendered 4D point clouds with temporally persistent static points.
MotionCtrl also supports object control; CineMaster ( Wang et al., 2025c ) uses 3D box layouts, and Diffusion as Shader ( Gu et al., 2025 ) uses 3D tracking videos for joint control.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
GenCine learns to generate a video from a reference image, a camera path,
and local foreground trajectories. Training controls are recovered from
videos; inference controls are supplied by the artist. Both pass through
the same three steps (Fig. 3 ): (i) Place the controls in each view. Project background and handle
points through the specified camera so the model knows where guidance
applies. (ii) Preserve identity and 3D motion. Use fixed handle colors to
identify regions across frames and separate XYZ maps to describe their
positions relative to the static scene. (iii) Learn to follow the guidance. Encode the maps with the
frozen video autoencoder and train adaptation modules on paired
videos, reference images, and controls.

blocks.en: 3.1 Scene Scaffold and Motion Authoring
blocks.zh: 3.1 场景脚手脚和动作写作

blocks.en: 3.2 Motion Representation: Correspondence Maps and Rigid Handles
blocks.zh: 3.2 代表动议: 函式地图和硬式操作

blocks.en: The motion representation in GenCine follows two principles: explicit correspondence and local rigidity. The first is motivated by motion correspondence in human visual perception ( Ullman, 1979 ; Dawson, 1991 ) ; the second allows a few local controls to approximate complex foreground deformation ( Sumner et al., 2007 ; Sorkine & Alexa, 2007 ) .
blocks.zh: 在GenCine中动议陈述遵循了两项原则:明确的函证和地方僵化. 第一种是以人类视觉感知中的运动通信为动机的(Ullman,1979;Dawson,1991;第二种允许一些局部控制来近似复杂的前地变形(Sumner等,2007;Sorkine & Alexa,2007.

blocks.en: • Preserving identity and 3D position. We encode world-space XYZ coordinates as RGB values. Static background coordinates provide position and persistent identity. For moving foreground points, we separate current XYZ from fixed colors identifying handles across frames (Fig. 4 ). • Rigid motion handles. Multiple independently controlled rigid handles approximate non-rigid motion—for example, moving a person’s hands while keeping the torso still. This provides local control without authoring a dense deformation field or requiring an object template, skeleton, or category-specific motion prior.

blocks.en: 3.3 Architecture
blocks.zh: 3.3 建筑

blocks.en: We build GenCine on a pretrained Wan video diffusion model and freeze its VAE and base diffusion weights. We train only a lightweight side branch for geometric guidance, convolutional projections between branches, and LoRA adapters in the main branch.
blocks.zh: 我们用预先训练过的Wan视频传播模型打造GenCine,并冻结其VAE和基础传播权重. 我们只训练一个轻量级的侧分机,用于几何指向,分机之间的演化预测,以及主分机中的LORA适配器.

blocks.en: The frozen VAE encodes all three guidance-map sequences. The main branch receives the noisy video latent, the reference-frame latent, and the encoded foreground identity sequence. The side branch receives all three encoded maps and binary masks marking valid background projections ( 𝐌 bg \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{bg}} ), projected handle pixels ( 𝐌 fg \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{fg}} ), and the first-frame dynamic region ( 𝐌 dyn \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{dyn}} ). It operates at half the main branch’s spatial resolution and injects features through zero-initialized residual projections. Supplementary Sec. E details mask processing, input layouts, and feature transfer.

Training videos contain observed motion but no artist-authored handles.
For real clips, we estimate depth and camera trajectories with
ViPE ( Huang et al., 2025 ) and obtain motion trajectories with
CoWTracker ( Lai et al., 2026 ) . Taking the first frame as
input, we use its dynamic mask to sample spatially separated handles
from visible foreground points with valid geometry. Each handle groups
nearby tracks within a scene-scaled 3D ball and follows their motion
through the clip.

blocks.en:
We build GenCine upon Wan2.1-Fun-V1.1-14B-Control ( Wan et al., 2025 ) . We only train a small set of adaptation modules to learn the proposed geometry guidance maps.
The model is trained for approximately 20 20 k iterations on 4 4 H100 GPUs.

该型号在4个H100GPU上为约20个20k的迭代所训练.

blocks.en:

motions. Approximately 5 5 k clips come from synthetic datasets,
including Dynamic Replica ( Karaev et al., 2023 ) and
PointOdyssey ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) , which provide ground-truth geometry
and motion trajectories. The remaining clips come from real-world
datasets, including SpatialVid-HQ ( Wang et al., 2025b ) . For these clips,
we estimate depth, camera poses, and dynamic masks using our geometry
extraction pipeline and obtain motion trajectories with
CoWTracker ( Lai et al., 2026 ) .
All clips are processed and cropped to 480 × 832 480\times 832 resolution.
We generate the missing video captions with Qwen2.5-VL-72B ( Bai et al., 2025 ) and encode them with umT5 ( Chung et al., 2023 ) .

We assess video quality using the subject consistency, background consistency,
and imaging quality metrics from VBench-I2V ( Huang et al., 2024 ) .

blocks.en:
We compare with Wan2.1 ( Wan et al., 2025 ) and five controllable video generation methods.
In our evaluation, ATI ( Wang et al., 2025a ) , Wan-Move ( Chu et al., 2025 ) ,
and Go-with-the-Track ( Namekata et al., 2026 ) receive dense 2D
foreground and background trajectories extracted from ground-truth videos.
VerseCrafter ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) and SymphoMotion ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) provide camera control and coarse object-level motion control.
GenCine uses sparse 3D motion handles and a target camera trajectory
derived from the same reference motion.
Dense ground-truth trajectories are unavailable when authoring new motion from
a single image; a similar input asymmetry is discussed in concurrent work ( Liu et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en: 5 Discussion
blocks.zh: 5 讨论情况

blocks.en:
We presented GenCine, a system for jointly
authoring camera and object motion in a shared 3D world lifted from a
single image. Its guidance maps encode static background coordinates,
persistent foreground handle identities, and current world-space
positions in a form compatible with pretrained video diffusion models.
This representation makes the intended 3D motion explicit where
image-space trajectories alone leave it ambiguous. Our results show
that a few local handles can compose camera and foreground motion,
including a piecewise-rigid approximation to articulated motion,
through lightweight adaptation of a pretrained video generator.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了GenCine,一种联合系统
在共享的 三维世界中 创建相机和物体运动
单相相相. 它的指导地图编码了静态背景坐标,
持久前景控件身份和当前世界空间
与预先训练的视频传播模型兼容的形式中的位置.
这种表述方式使预期的三维动议明确了:
图像空间轨迹本身就使其模糊不清。 我们的结果显示
几把本地手柄可以制作相机和前地运动,
包括一个片状硬化的近似来表达运动,
通过轻量级的改造 预先训练的视频生成器。

blocks.en:
The single-image scaffold leaves occluded regions unmodeled, requiring
the generator to synthesize unseen surfaces under large viewpoint
changes. Local rigid handles are better suited to articulated motion
than to fracture, tearing, or fluid dynamics, and authoring many handles
can become cumbersome for distributed deformation. Independently
authored handles also impose no physical constraints or causal
interactions between objects. Geometry completion, automatic handle
placement, and learned interaction priors could extend the range of
shots artists can compose.

对于分布式变形来说,它会变得繁琐. 独立
作者手柄也没有施加任何物理限制或因果

blocks.en:
Fig. 7 examines an edit that moves a teapot
toward the camera while preserving its orientation in world space.
Image-plane trajectories constrain projected motion but do not uniquely
specify the underlying 3D transformation. In this example, Wan-Move produces
geometrically inconsistent motion across the sampled frames. In GenCine, 3D handles
specify the intended displacement in the canonical world frame, and the
generated sequence better preserves the teapot’s orientation and scene geometry.
This example illustrates the benefit of making the intended 3D motion explicit
when different spatial motions can have similar image-plane projections.

blocks.en: The artist loads a single image into the Blender interface for GenCine. The system constructs the scene scaffold once from estimated depth, camera intrinsics, and the dynamic mask. blocks.zh: 附录H 失败案件和限制

blocks.en: Monocular depth estimation can fail on reflective or transparent surfaces and thin structures. Errors in the lifted point cloud propagate to the background XYZ map and can cause geometric inconsistencies during viewpoint changes. Even with accurate visible geometry, the single-image scaffold leaves occluded surfaces unmodeled; the generator must synthesize them as they become visible.
blocks.zh: 单体深度估计在反射或透明地表和薄结构上可能失败. 被解除点云出错会传播到背景 XYZ 映射中,在视距变化时可能造成几何不一致. 即使有准确可见的几何图案,单像脚手架也留下了未被模型化的外表;生成器必须在它们变得可见后合成.

blocks.en: Each authored handle moves its selected points as a rigid group. Multiple handles can approximate articulated motion, but fracture, tearing, and fluid dynamics remain difficult. More handles allow finer control at the cost of additional authoring effort. Independently authored handles impose neither physical constraints nor causal interactions between objects, as discussed in Sec. 5 .
blocks.zh: 每个被作者的手柄会以刚性组的形式移动其选定的点. 多个手柄可以近似地表达出运动,但断裂,撕裂和流体动力学仍然很困难. 更多的手柄允许更精细的控制,而代价是额外的编写工作. 如第5节所讨论,独立作者的手柄既没有施加物理限制,也没有施加物体之间的因果关系。

blocks.en: Both XYZ maps use the first-frame scene bounding box (Eq. 9 ). Points within this box map to [ 0 , 1 ] 3 [0,1]^{3} , but a handle driven outside it can produce foreground XYZ values outside this range. Authoring within the scene extent keeps the guidance values in the RGB range; we expose the per-axis scale to the artist in the UI as a visual cue.
